newsitem.title: USA: World Bank approves China power project loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves China power project loan.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday it had approved a $400 million loan to China for the $1.2 billion Inner Mongolia Thermal Power Project.

The loan, approved on Tuesday, will be at the bank's standard interest rate for LIBOR-based U.S. dollar single currency loans, with a maturity of 20 years that includes a five-year grace period, the bank said in a statement.
Of the $400 million loan, $330 million will be used in the building of the coal-burning Tuoketuo power station, and $70 million will be used for a second-phase distribution project.

The project aims to increase energy efficiency, promote power sector reform and private sector development, and boost economic development in Tuoketuo county in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, the statement said.
Tuoketuo has an abundance of coal reserves and prime power generation sites, and is well-suited to servicing densely populated Beijing, Tianjian and Tangshan, the bank said.
